sections.heading: Welcome back
brief: School is back after an 11-week summer
A newsletter comes at the start of every month through May
Read the announcements, reminders and calendar each month
paragraphs: Welcome back for another school year at Burlington Montessori School! We hope everyone was able to enjoy this summer; it was a lot of fun having 11 weeks instead of the usual 10. Our friends that attended summer camp had a lot of fun doing different activities every day. There is so much to look forward to this year!

This is the first monthly newsletter for the year, please expect one at the beginning of each month through May (the last one is a combined May/June newsletter). I do my best to send these out on the 1st of each month but occasionally they will come on the 2nd or 3rd if the first falls on a weekend. It is important to read through the announcements, reminders and the monthly calendar so you do not miss anything.

sections.heading: Snack calendar
brief: Every family signs up for one snack day a month
Half days still need a morning snack
See the snack and allergy email for what to bring
paragraphs: Everyone needs to sign up for their turn on the snack calendar. It is posted in the entryway of the school, Classroom 1 beginning on the left. We ask that all parents sign up once per month to keep things fair. If you sign up for other months in advance, please make note of it in your calendar a day or two ahead of time because parents do occasionally forget. Beneath the September calendar, there are October, November and December calendars. The days off for kids are crossed off. We still need snack on half days, but we only need enough for morning snack because all kids leave by 11:30. Check the snack and allergy email for more details.

sections.heading: Blue bags and nap bags
brief: Bring blue bags and nap bags on Mondays
Blue bags come home every other Friday; nap bags every Friday
Keep napping items out of the blue bag
paragraphs: Please bring your child’s blue bag and napping bags (if needed) on Mondays. Blue bags will go home every other Friday, not every week, please return them on the following Monday. Nap bags go home every Friday unless your child missed school that day. Please do not send napping items in the blue bag! Blue bags are stored away from the nap bags.

sections.heading: Pickup times
brief: Pickup times are strict
Late pickups are charged a late fee
paragraphs: We are also reminding parents that your pickup times are strict, and we are enforcing late fees for late pickups.

sections.heading: Car line
brief: Bring a paper sign with your child’s first name
Hold it out the window if there’s glare
Dismissal runs 3:00–3:05 in two lines
Pull up to the next set of stairs before unbuckling
paragraphs: During the car line, it helps at the beginning of the year to have a paper sign with your child’s first name on it. Something large enough to be seen from the dashboard or window of your car from a good distance away. If you see the teacher struggling with the afternoon glare, please hold the sign out the window! Sometimes, the afternoon glare can make your face and sign invisible to us, even though I see everyone at the door each morning and know who you are. Our goal is to have dismissal begin at 3:00 and be done no later than 3:05. There should be two lines side-by-side. The first few days have been smooth so far. I’ve noticed the line reaching the street again, please pull up at least to the next set of stairs to get out and buckle your child. It helps keep the line moving.

sections.heading: Show and Tell
brief: Show and tell is on Wednesdays
Bring something your child made — not a store-bought toy
It’s optional; don’t push a child who isn’t ready
paragraphs: Each classroom does show and tell on Wednesdays. Your child will bring something that they worked on (a project) like a drawing, story or a Lego, a book, etc. This is to help the child to stand up in the class in front of their friends to present their creation. Toys bought from the store do not help us achieve this in the best way possible, and we ask that those are kept out of the school anyway. It was great to see some students bring a show and tell Wednesday! It is optional, so please don’t force the kids to bring something in if they aren’t ready right away. We usually get most kids participating after the first couple of months. It is best if they only bring something in when they want to and are free to sit in the group and watch show and tell without presenting.

sections.heading: Birthdays
brief: No goodie bags for birthdays
Donate a book to the class instead
Email the office about a week ahead
paragraphs: I forgot to add in the parent meeting memo that you should not bring in goodie bags for the class for your child’s birthday. At BMS, we encourage you to donate a book to the class which we keep here. We will write in your child’s birthday and name to mark the special occasion. When it is close to your child’s birthday, their teacher or myself will reach out to give you the specific details. It is best to send me an email about a week or so before so we can make sure there is no conflict with another birthday or school event.

sections.heading: This month
brief: No extra days off in September after Labor Day
September is for settling into the routine
Consistent attendance and arriving before 8:30 help all year
paragraphs: After the general announcements and reminders, we have a calendar of monthly events and days off from school.

In September, we do not have any extra days off for holidays after Labor Day. This month is all about introducing the new students to our schedule/work, reintroducing the returning students to our routines and establishing our classroom cultures before we dive into all of the fun events of the school year. Consistent attendance in September pays dividends throughout the year. The consistency of the schedule helps all of the kids adjust for the entire school year. We have done a good job so far this week getting to school before 8:30, and I promise the drop offs get easier as the year goes along.

curriculumIntro: The final part of the newsletter is our monthly curriculum. These are the wide-ranging topics covered throughout the month in various different ways. This will help guide you through a little bit of what your kids recount from their school day or through the pictures you see on homeroom. Due to the schedule of some months, you may see a topic continued from the previous month in future newsletters.
